What that project could not find out is absent here too.

-0.13000,51.50000.name: United Kingdom — Home Office — licensed establishments and annual procedures
-0.13000,51.50000.desc: Every UK establishment licensed to use animals in research is named in a public list, alongside annual procedure counts by species, severity and purpose. It is the only place in the world where both the places and the numbers are public and complete, and it exists because Parliament legislated for it in 1986 rather than because anyone offered it.

-97.82000,30.50830.name: ViaGen Pets & Equine
-97.82000,30.50830.state: Cedar Park, Texas — 1108 Cottonwood Creek Trail
-97.82000,30.50830.desc: Clones pets and horses for anyone who pays, at around fifty thousand dollars for a dog. No biosafety rule applies at any point, because nothing foreign is inserted and the regulations only trigger on inserted material. It is also the company that produced cloned Przewalski’s horses for conservation programmes — so the capability now used to rescue an endangered subspecies exists because a consumer market paid to develop it first.

-71.08700,42.36500.name: Indigo Ag
-71.08700,42.36500.desc: Sells microbial seed treatments and runs a carbon-credit programme for farmers, valued in the billions and repeatedly restructured. The pairing is unusual: the same company sells an engineered input and certifies the environmental benefit claimed from using it, and the certification market has no independent verifier of comparable scale.

80.32000,26.46700.name: National Centre of Organic and Natural Farming (India) — biofertiliser standards
80.32000,26.46700.state: Ghaziabad — Hapur Road, Kamla Nehru Nagar
80.32000,26.46700.desc: Sets the standards for microbial inoculants sold to Indian farmers, in a market of millions of smallholders where a bag of live bacteria is cheaper than fertiliser. Quality control on living products sold this widely is where biosafety and consumer protection turn out to be the same problem.

-77.03690,38.90720.name: USDA APHIS Wildlife Services
-77.03690,38.90720.desc: The manufacturer sells this vaccine only to government agencies running rabies control programmes; no private buyer can obtain it. Distribution is by state and federal wildlife services, and the public-facing instruction where baits land in gardens and streets is to leave them alone and telephone a control programme. That structure is worth noting precisely because it is unusual on this map: an engineered organism released into the open where the release is planned by a public agency, the product cannot be bought, and a member of the public who finds one is given a number to call. Most releases documented here have none of those three features.

-74.17240,40.73570.name: Merck Animal Health
-74.17240,40.73570.state: Rahway, New Jersey — Merck Animal Health
-74.17240,40.73570.desc: The Innovax line puts the Newcastle disease fusion protein gene into a turkey herpesvirus vector, so a vaccinated bird develops immunity to Marek's disease from the vector itself and to Newcastle from the insert. Later products in the line carry two antigens at once. The reason multi-antigen constructs exist is worth stating plainly, because it is a fact about engineered organisms rather than about marketing: giving a bird two different recombinant herpesvirus vaccines is not recommended, because the faster-replicating one can neutralise the slower and compromise both. Engineered viruses given to the same animal compete with each other, and the industry solved that by combining the inserts rather than by using fewer vectors.

-74.17240,40.73570.name: Synbio Technologies
-74.17240,40.73570.state: Monmouth Junction, New Jersey — with operations in Nanjing
-74.17240,40.73570.desc: A gene synthesis company operating across the United States and China, and a member of the industry's voluntary screening consortium. Its published capability is the reason it belongs here: synthesis to lengths of 200 kilobases, whole small genomes assembled through yeast, and — stated on its own product page — arbitrary synthesis of adenovirus genomes. An adenovirus genome is the backbone of the vector vaccines elsewhere on this map. When the capability to write a viral genome to order is a catalogue item rather than a national programme, the constraint on who can build an engineered organism stops being technical and becomes whatever the screening protocol catches.
